resources.string: On at boot, and nothing outside the VPN
Android reports these settings only while the VPN runs. Connect once to see them here.
Off. The VPN starts only when you start it, and traffic goes direct whenever it is down.
Always-on is set: the VPN starts at boot and restarts if it stops. Block connections without VPN is off, so traffic can go direct in the gap before it is up.
Always-on and Block connections without VPN are both set. Nothing leaves this phone except through the chain, from boot, with or without a data connection.
In VPN settings, tap the gear next to SocksChain and turn on Always-on VPN, then Block connections without VPN.
With Block connections without VPN on, apps left out of the chain get no network at all.
With Block connections without VPN on, Android may block the local network this chain leaves out.
No chains yet. A chain is an ordered list of proxies your traffic passes through, one inside the next.
Traffic reaches each hop through the ones above it. The last hop is where it leaves for the internet.
Built-in Tor: three relays, then the internet. Sites see a Tor exit.
Built-in Tor. The hops below are reached through Tor, so they never see your address, and the last one is where you appear to be.
Built-in Tor, reached through the hops above: Tor itself connects through them, which helps where Tor is blocked. Sites see a Tor exit.
Built-in Tor. Tor connects through the hops above; the hops below are reached through Tor.
Asked over TCP from the last hop, so lookups follow the chain too.
Home devices, printers and the router stay reachable directly.

Free proxies are run by strangers. Some log what passes through, some are honeypots, and some are machines whose owners never meant to run one. Each result here has passed a TLS check, so it cannot read or change your HTTPS traffic, but it still sees where you connect. Put them after Tor, so they never see your address, and not in front of anything you log in to.
List hosts and proxies see a Tor exit, not you. Slower, and times include Tor.
Connect to see traffic. Nothing is recorded while the VPN is off, and the record goes when it stops: it is only ever held in memory.
Not identified (refused before Android could say)
Apps on the left, where they connect on the right; thicker lines carried more. Tap a destination to block it.

A domain blocks itself and every name under it; an IP or CIDR range blocks those addresses whatever name they came by. Domain blocks cannot catch apps that bring their own encrypted DNS; address blocks can.
